record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: For the 4-colored graph construction of closed Heegaard genus two 3-manifolds from 6-tuples (n_1, h_1; n_2, h_2; n_3, h_3), find arithmetic conditions on the six integers that are exactly those yielding homology 3-spheres.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and construction. A 4-colored graph is a finite multigraph $G=(V,E)$ together with an edge-coloring $\gamma:E	o\{0,1,2,3\}$ such that at every vertex the four edges incident to it carry the four distinct colors. From such a graph one builds a 3-dimensional pseudocomplex $K(G)$ by taking one tetrahedron $\sigma_v$ for each vertex $v\in V$, labeling the four 2-faces of $\sigma_v$ by the colors $0,1,2,3$, and gluing the $c$-labeled faces of $\sigma_v$ and $\sigma_w$ whenever $v$ and $w$ are joined by a $c$-colored edge. If $|K(G)|$ is a closed 3-manifold, $G$ is called a crystallization (or gem) of that manifold.

It is known that every closed orientable 3-manifold of Heegaard genus at most two admits a 4-colored graph representation that is determined by a 6-tuple of integers
$$ (n_1,h_1;\; n_2,h_2;\; n_3,h_3) $$
subject to the conditions $n_i\ge 1$ and $0\le h_i\le n_i-1$ for $i=1,2,3$, via the following standard construction. Take three disjoint cycles of lengths $2n_1,2n_2,2n_3$ formed alternately by edges of colors $0$ and $1$, and attach edges of colors $2$ and $3$ according to cyclic permutations determined by the shifts $h_1,h_2,h_3$, yielding a regular 4-colored graph $G(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ of order $2(n_1+n_2+n_3)$ which (when it represents a manifold) is a crystallization of a closed orientable 3-manifold $M(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ of Heegaard genus at most two.

Problem. Determine necessary and sufficient arithmetic conditions on the integers $(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ (with $n_i\ge 1$ and $0\le h_i<n_i$) so that the resulting 3-manifold $M(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ is an integral homology 3-sphere, i.e. $H_1(M;\mathbb{Z})=0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question asks for explicit arithmetic conditions on the 6-tuple parameters characterizing homology 3-spheres among genus-two crystallizations. The available literature describes algorithms and enumerations producing homology spheres from 6-tuples, but no closed-form arithmetic characterization of exactly which 6-tuples yield homology 3-spheres was located. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Graphs encoding 3-manifolds of genus 2
status_evidence.snippet: All closed connected orientable 3-manifolds of genus 2 can be represented by crystallizations uniquely defined by 6-tuples of integers satisfying simple arithmetic conditions.
status_evidence.claim: 6-tuple representation of genus-2 3-manifolds is a known framework, but the specific arithmetic characterization of homology spheres is not stated.

status_evidence.title: Three-manifolds with Heegaard genus at most two represented by crystallisations
status_evidence.snippet: Computer enumeration of 6-tuples giving crystallizations of low complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Enumeration approach is used; no general arithmetic homology-sphere criterion is given.
